title: How to Build Deep Friendships as an Adult
excerpt: Most adults are lonely and would never say so. Friendship does not happen to grown-ups by accident anymore. You have to build it on purpose.
body:
When you were young, friendship was nearly free. You were thrown together, in classrooms and dorms and on teams, in the same place at the same time week after week, and depth happened without anyone deciding it would. Then you grew up, and the shared space disappeared. Now everyone is busy, scattered across the city, drowning in obligations, and the friendships that used to grow on their own require something they never required before. They require intention. Most adults never make the switch, which is why so many of us are quietly lonely and would die before admitting it.

## Admit that proximity is gone

The first thing to accept is that the old conditions are not coming back. You will not stumble into a best friend at the office the way you did in college, not usually, because adult life does not provide the repeated, unhurried proximity that depth needs. If you wait for friendship to happen to you, you will wait alone.

So you have to manufacture the proximity that life no longer hands you. This sounds unromantic, scheduling friendship like a dentist appointment, and it feels that way at first. But every deep adult friendship I have is one I or the other person chose to keep showing up for, on purpose, when it would have been easier not to. The spontaneity is a lie we tell ourselves. The showing up is the real thing.

## Choose a few and go deep

The culture pushes width, a wide network of acquaintances, hundreds of contacts, dozens of people you wave to. Scripture pushes depth. Jesus had crowds, but he had twelve, and inside the twelve he had three. He did not try to be close to everyone. Neither should you.

Pick a small number of people and invest disproportionately in them. Depth requires repetition, the same people over a long time, which means you cannot do it with everyone. Choosing a few is not a failure to love widely. It is the only way anyone has ever loved deeply. A friend who sticks closer than a brother (Proverbs 18:24) is not a friend you found by networking. It is one you made by staying.

## Go first, and go past the surface

Adult friendship stalls at the weather. Two men can know each other for a decade and never get past sports and work, because someone has to go first into the real conversation and nobody wants to be the one who makes it weird. Be the one who makes it weird. Ask the question under the question. Say the true thing about how you are actually doing.

Friendship deepens at the speed of disclosure. When you risk telling someone something real, you give them permission to do the same, and the relationship can move. Stay safe, and it stays shallow forever. The vulnerability has to go first, and it usually has to be you, because everyone is waiting for someone else to make it safe.

## Build it around something

The strongest adult friendships are usually built around a shared thing, not just a shared feeling. Men especially tend to bond shoulder to shoulder, working on a project, rather than face to face, talking about feelings. So give the friendship a structure. A standing breakfast. A project. A small group that actually meets. A workout. Serving together at church.

The structure carries the friendship through the dry weeks when neither of you feels like it, and the dry weeks are exactly when most adult friendships quietly die. Two believers who confess sin to each other and pray (James 5:16) have a structure stronger than mood, and mood is not strong enough to sustain anything over years.

## This week

Text one person you would like to be closer to and propose something specific and recurring, a monthly breakfast, a weekly walk, not a vague let us hang out sometime. Then, the next time someone asks how you are, tell the truth instead of saying fine. Go first.

Friendship will not happen to you anymore. You are an adult, and the free version expired. But the built version, chosen and tended on purpose, is deeper than anything proximity ever gave you for free.
